description: AI Incident Diagnosis Agent evaluation set (Golden Dataset): fault injection creates known root causes (ground truth) used to score LLM output during tuning. Used to measure (not train).
evaluation_metric: expected_root_cause_keywords hit rate + confidence calibration + parse success rate + cost/latency

traffic.note: orders endpoint throws RuntimeException and returns 500 in error mode
all requests sleep 2-5s, so p99 necessarily exceeds the 1s threshold
FaultState internal thread allocates 10MB per second without releasing, triggering G1 Old Gen > 85%
two faults injected simultaneously: error returns 500, latency sleeps all requests 2-5s

cases.evaluation_note: discrimination: both independent root causes must be identified. The HighErrorRate incident must hit the error keywords (not be pulled toward latency by the p99 spike); the HighLatency incident must hit the latency keywords (not be pulled toward error by 500/RuntimeException logs)

traffic.note: latency request delays and the memory leak thread occur at the same time

cases.evaluation_note: discrimination: the HighLatency incident must hit the latency keywords (not pulled by the heap spike); the HighMemoryUsage incident must hit the memory keywords (not pulled by sleeping logs)

traffic.note: error returns 500 and the memory leak thread occurs at the same time

cases.evaluation_note: discrimination: the HighErrorRate incident must hit the error keywords (not pulled by the heap spike); the HighMemoryUsage incident must hit the memory keywords (not pulled by 500 logs)

traffic.note: createOrder calls the simulated payment-service; it times out after 3000ms -> 502 Bad Gateway, counted into 5xx -> fires HighErrorRate

cases.evaluation_note: same alert name as case-001 but a DIFFERENT root-cause class: the symptom (5xx) is local, the cause is the downstream dependency. Must NOT diagnose pool exhaustion / RuntimeException. Logs show the call chain: 'Calling payment-service' then 'payment-service request timed out'.

traffic.note: downstream 502s and latency sleeps occur at the same time

cases.evaluation_note: discrimination: HighErrorRate must cite the downstream timeout (not the latency sleep); HighLatency must cite latency (not the 502s). Cross-category pair.

traffic.note: downstream 502s and the memory-leak thread occur at the same time

cases.evaluation_note: discrimination: HighErrorRate must cite the downstream timeout (not the heap spike); HighMemoryUsage must cite heap (not the 502s).

inject.note: no fault injected; a synthetic test alert is sent via POST /api/alert/test so the agent analyzes a NORMAL service

cases.evaluation_note: anti-false-positive control: with no fault, the agent must NOT invent a root cause; low confidence (<0.5) and 'no anomaly / insufficient evidence' is the CORRECT output.

inject.note: error fault injected first and its alerts complete, then stopped; latency injected immediately after so the error's RuntimeException logs remain inside the Loki correlation window

traffic.note: phase 1 exercises orders (500s), phase 2 exercises products (sleeps)

cases.evaluation_note: temporal isolation: the HighLatency analysis window still contains the previous error's RuntimeException logs (Loki retention). Retrieval-layer exclusion (LogQL != RuntimeException for non-error-rate) must keep them out; the root cause must stay latency, never error.

inject.note: downstream fault first (leaves 'payment-service request timed out' ERROR logs), stopped; then error fault injected - its 5xx analysis window contains the stale downstream logs

cases.evaluation_note: LLM-layer discrimination under contamination: stale downstream logs sit inside the HighErrorRate context (error-rate does not exclude them at retrieval). The agent must recognize them as a competing/leftover signal and keep the root cause on the pool exhaustion, optionally reporting the downstream logs in competing_signals_observed.
